entry.title: [Economía] La ganancia de Procter & Gamble cae por debajo de las expectativas con volumen invariado
entry.summary:
Procter & Gamble informó resultados mixtos en el cuarto trimestre, debido a una demanda insuficiente de sus productos lo que resultó en ventas inferiores a las esperadas. entry.title: [Economía] Nike pierde un tercio de sus ventas en China debido a la competencia local.
entry.summary:

La empresa había sido una de las regiones más rápidas de crecimiento para Nike, pero ahora es la más pequeña y se considera un obstáculo para el restablecimiento global. La tendencia "China Chic" ha llevado a los jóvenes chinos a preferir marcas nacionales sobre marcas extranjeras como Nike. Los consumidores buscan una selección de productos locales, en lugar de copias de productos que se producen en otros lugares del mundo. Además, la distribución de Nike en China es criticada por ser compleja y basada en descuentos. La empresa ha nombrado a Cathy Sparks como vicepresidenta y gerente general de China, quien afirma que Nike está tomando las medidas necesarias para conectar con los consumidores chinos. La tendencia "China Chic" ha cambiado el mercado de zapatos, ya que los consumidores buscan productos más locales y personalizados. Nike había replicado su estrategia global en China, pero ahora se da cuenta de que necesita adaptarse a las necesidades específicas del mercado chino.

Esto se debe en gran medida a que los jóvenes chinos están cada vez más atraídos por marcas locales, lo que ha llevado a la aparición del movimiento "China Chic", caracterizado por una búsqueda de conexiones y experiencias más locales y personalizadas. entry.title: [Data Science] How Much Does a Local LLM Actually Cost to Run? I Measured Every Watt on Apple Silicon
entry.summary:
No tengo un 3090. Corro todo en un Mac Studio M3 Ultra con 96 GB de memoria unificada—sin GPU discreta, ni VRAM, solo una sola poola de memoria que comparte el procesador y la GPU. Eso es lo suficientemente diferente como para querer saber si el mismo sorprendimiento se mantiene, y en qué medida. Por lo tanto, lo medí. Mi modelo de 120 billones de parámetros cuesta aproximadamente cinco veces menos por token que un modelo con un cuarto de su tamaño. Lee los contadores del SoC a través de la interfaz IOReport de Apple—los mismos que se utilizan en el tablero de energía de Activity Monitor—which significa no sudo, ni instrumentación externa, solo los números que el chip informa sobre sí mismo. 🤖 Análisis generado por IA: El autor de este artículo compara el rendimiento energético de diferentes modelos de inteligencia artificial en un Mac Studio con procesador Apple Silicon, específicamente en una configuración de 96 GB de memoria unificada. El objetivo era determinar si la sorpresa observada en los modelos de Intel se repite en Apple Silicon y cuánto es mayor. Los resultados sugieren que el mismo fenómeno ocurre, pero con un impacto aún más significativo. La herramienta utilizada para medir el consumo energético fue una herramienta personalizada llamada TokenWatt, que utiliza la interfaz de Apple para leer los contadores de potencia del SoC y calcular el costo de cada token en función de su velocidad de generación y el consumo energético. Esto se debe a que el consumo energético del modelo más grande es menor que el de algunos modelos más pequeños, lo que permite una mayor velocidad de generación y un costo más bajo. El modelo más grande utiliza todas las 96 GB de memoria unificada del Mac Studio, lo que aumenta significativamente el consumo energético y reduce la velocidad de generación. En conclusión, este artículo destaca la importancia de considerar el impacto energético en la elección de modelos de inteligencia artificial, especialmente en entornos donde se busca minimizar el consumo energético. Los resultados sugieren que los modelos más grandes pueden ser más económicos que los modelos más pequeños, lo que puede tener implicaciones significativas para las aplicaciones que requieren procesamiento de gran cantidad de datos.

entry.summary:
The following article originally appeared on LinkedIn and is being republished here with the author’s permission.
We’re currently at the peak of the hype cycle. On June 7, Peter Steinberger posted that you shouldn’t be prompting coding agents anymore ; you should be designing loops that prompt your agents. That same week, Boris Cherny of Anthropic said on stage that he doesn’t prompt Claude anymore: “I write loops; the loops do the work .” Addy Osmani published an essay called “ Loop Engineering ” on June 7, swyx published “ Loopcraft: The Art of Stacking Loops ” on June 12, and LangChain published “ The Art of Loop Engineering ” on June 16. Then came the AI Engineer World’s Fair, where the word dominated the main stage . Swyx’s keynote was about Loopcraft, an entire track was devoted to software factories, speaker after speaker reached for the same word, and the conference closed on July 2 with an hour-long debate about whether the hype behind loops has outrun what works in practice. The problem is that the people talking about loops aren’t all discussing the same thing. I counted at least four distinct architectures hiding behind that one word. So this post is an attempt to map out what everyone means. The execution loop: The agent’s own act-observe cycle This is the loop most people picture when they say “agent”: call a tool, read the result, decide the next action, and repeat until there are no more tool calls to make. It’s what Addy calls the inner execution loop, the part agents can now run largely on their own, and it’s the innermost loop you can engineer. (swyx’s stack has a token loop, but nobody designs the token loop. It’s just part of the model.) Swyx’s original Loopcraft diagram The execution loop iterates on steps within one task. It ends on environment feedback: the test output, the API response, and the file contents. Humans are usually absent mid-loop and appear at the boundaries, approving plans or reviewing results. The execution loop also ends whenever the agent decides it’s done, whether or not it actually is. The first fix the field found for that was to wrap this loop in another one that doesn’t take the agent’s word for it. The task loop: Restart the agent until the spec is satisfied This was the first loop to get a name and it’s Geoffrey Huntley’s Ralph loop, which got name-checked from the AI Engineer World’s Fair main stage when Allie Howe of Keycard introduced the software factories track by citing Geoffrey’s article “ Everything Is a Ralph Loop .” A Ralph loop restarts a coding agent against the same specification over and over, allocating a completely fresh context window every iteration and doing exactly one task per loop. The apparent waste is the point: Refeeding the full spec each time prevents the context rot and compaction events that quietly degrade long-running sessions. What this loop iterates on is a single artifact. What ends the loop is spec compliance and passing tests. entry.title: [Data Science] Avoiding Entity Key Drift in a Data Lake: Step 1, Normalization
entry.summary:
This is the opening piece of a four-part deep dive series, on building a high-frequency streaming pipeline against a live public API. The data source is openSenseMap, a citizen-science IoT network used for climate research, mostly in Germany. A live public API is what makes it useful: it produces data-quality problems and edge cases that clean sample datasets never show. This article focuses on step-1: Normalization, later pieces cover matching algorithms, adaptive polling and noise filtering, and a vendor-agnostic Apache Iceberg pipeline with Terraform that runs locally in Docker and moves to AWS or GCP with minimal change. The narrative around generative AI is shifting in 2026. While massive frontier models keep grabbing headlines, the reality of enterprise AI deployment looks very different. Ranging from 1 billion to 10 billion parameters, SLMs run efficiently on local hardware, edge devices, and affordable GPUs, while still packing in remarkable capabilities. If you're a data professional, knowing how to select, fine-tune, and deploy these compact models is no longer optional. It's a core engineering requirement. Why spend thousands of dollars on cloud API calls for a narrow data-extraction task when an optimized 3-billion-parameter model can execute it instantly on a local server? ChaitanyaK77's open-source Jupyter Notebook repository is a step-by-step guide for training a compact model using the lightweight TinyStories dataset. It strips away the complex abstractions of modern frameworks, pushing you to engage directly with the raw mechanics of model training. entry.summary:
Lando Norris believes he is driving better than during his title-winning 2025 Formula 1 campaign Fresh from securing pole position and a commanding victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix, reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris believes he is performing at an even higher level than he did during his championship-winning 2025 season. Norris dominated the weekend at the Hungaroring, taking pole on Saturday before converting it into a convincing victory on Sunday. While the result underlined McLaren's pace, the Briton suggested his own driving has also reached a new level. Asked whether he feels he is driving better than he did during last year's title-winning campaign, Norris admitted that Sunday's performance ranked among the very best of his Formula 1 career. "Right now, today, I would probably say it was up there with one of my best performances, in terms of extracting performance out of the car and being so close to the limit every single lap," Norris said. "So close that the team had to ask me to peg it back a little bit." Despite winning the championship last season, Norris believes he has continued to improve as a driver, even if the results have not always reflected that progress. "Honestly, although it kind of hurts me saying it because it doesn't mean that you just win, I feel like I'm doing a better job this year than I was last year, and I have done for a little while," he explained. "I've said that for a while. It just doesn't mean you win the races." The Hungarian Grand Prix, however, provided Norris with the opportunity to demonstrate what he believes he is capable of when both driver and car are operating at their best. "So, today, when we had a car, I think the words when I said, 'I think my performance is some of my best,' today proved exactly that: that I could go out and win very convincingly and be on pole in a good car." Norris credited his progress to months of work with his engineers, both during race weekends and away from the circuit, rather than any dramatic breakthrough. "So, yeah, I'm doing a better job, and that's because of working in many different areas, some away from the track with my team and some here at the track as well." "Just working in as many areas as possible. A lot of small differences add up, and you see the result today."

Red Bull admits budget cap will slow its F1 development in remainder of 2026 Laurent Mekies says his team has already introduced a large number of upgrades during the first half of the F1 season to reduce its deficit; Red Bull intends to shift focus to 2027 earlier than last year Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Liam Fabre Red Bull heads into the Formula 1 summer break fourth in the constructors' championship, but that does not tell the whole story. Since the season opener in Melbourne, the Milton Keynes-based team has made significant progress. Figures from data partner Paceteq show that Red Bull was as much as 1.3 seconds per lap down in terms of outright race pace in both Australia and China, meaning it was fighting with the likes of Haas and Alpine. Over the final two race weekends before the summer break, that deficit was reduced to just two to three tenths per lap. This shows that Red Bull has found around one second relative to the front of the field, but that has come at a price – both literally and figuratively. The team introduced two major upgrade packages in Miami and Austria, significantly revising its aerodynamic concept (with the sidepods, among other things, taking on a completely different appearance) while also eliminating the RB22's excess weight. While Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff questioned how Ferrari was seemingly able to introduce “unlimited” upgrades, the Scuderia pointed out that Red Bull may actually have brought even more new parts over the opening 11 race weekends of the year. Heading into the summer break, Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies admits it will be difficult for his team to maintain that rate of development during the second half of the season. That is naturally linked to F1's budget cap, which has been set at $215million this year. "We have brought a huge amount of development to the car between race one and here, in order to try to as soon as possible correct the large deficit we initially had," Mekies said. Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images "And it's probably difficult to imagine that we will continue at that rhythm. But we nonetheless need to see what is the best way to try and close these last three tenths." Mekies has previously explained that those final two to three tenths are the hardest to find, particularly because the competition is not standing still either. Has Red Bull learned from last year? Alongside the cost cap, all teams have another important decision to make: how to divide resources such as wind tunnel time between this year's car and next season's challenger. Mekies says Red Bull is taking a different approach in that respect compared to last year. Back then, the team threw everything at closing the gap to McLaren and giving Max Verstappen a chance to fight for a fifth world title, something Red Bull paid the price for at the start of 2026, technical director Pierre Wache later said. This year, Red Bull intends to shift its focus to the following season earlier: "I don't know about the other guys, but what is sure is that at some stage we'll need to make a call on the balance between this year and next year. "I expect that to happen earlier than what we have done last year, especially as the regulations are what they are." Esa forma determina el papel biológico de una proteína. Unas consolas retro Nintendo Famicombox funcionales fueron descubiertas en un hotel de amor japonés. En 1986, Nintendo lanzó una versión comercial del sistema 8-bit Famicom llamada Nintendo Famicombox, diseñada para almacenar hasta 16 cartuchos de juegos, lo que facilitaba el cambio entre títulos. Se utilizaba principalmente en hoteles y se podía acceder a los juegos pagando con monedas o mediante un sistema de pago por tiempo de juego. Estas consolas son muy raras. Un famoso archivista de Famicom llamado "Orochi" descubrió varias unidades funcionales en un hotel de amor japonés, excepto una. Orochi y su equipo investigaron el hotel y encontraron que la mayoría de las consolas estaban funcionando correctamente, aunque algunas juegos de disparos no podían ser jugados debido a la falta de compatibilidad con televisores LCD y el Zapper. El Famicombox utiliza controles NES en lugar de los controles exclusivos de Japón para Famicom. Orochi no reveló el nombre del hotel donde se encontraron las consolas, sugiriendo que quiere protegerlas. Antes de buscar Famicomboxes, asegúrate de investigar sobre los hoteles de amor japoneses.

La propuesta en sí misma es muy sencilla: queremos agregar las atributas de acción y método a los botones. <button action="/begin" method="GET">Start</button> Los Button Actions son tan simples que a menudo se pregunta por qué necesitan. La respuesta descansa en una distinción que los usuarios web intuyen pero rara vez tienen que pensar directamente: la diferencia entre un botón y un enlace. Se agregó una sección detallada "Buttons vs Links" a la propuesta, pero creo que merece una explicación de estilo blog para que la mayoría de las existentes no estén mal. Los enlaces representan un destino mientras que los botones representan una acción. Funcionalmente, esto significa que los enlaces permiten a los usuarios controlar el contexto en el que se abre, mientras que los botones no. Los navegadores ofrecen numerosas facilidades para re-contextualizar un enlace. Al hacer clic o taponar el enlace, se navega al destino correspondiente. Sin embargo, esta medida genera muchas preguntas, como ¿por qué necesitamos botones con acciones y métodos si ya existen enlaces que pueden realizar tareas similares? La clave reside en la distinción entre botones y enlaces, que representan dos tipos de interacciones diferentes. Los enlaces se utilizan para navegar a un destino específico, mientras que los botones se utilizan para realizar una acción dentro de un contexto determinado. Esto significa que los enlaces ofrecen una mayor flexibilidad en términos de re-contextualización, lo que permite a los usuarios controlar el contexto en el que se abre la página. A pesar de tener solo ocho comandos, es Turing-completa - o sea, en teoría, se puede computar cualquier cosa que cualquier otra lengua computa.
